chunks: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام used to recite five takbirs at a time. When people reached him, they would say, ‘O Commander of the Faithful, we did not catch the salat over Sahl ibn Hunayf,’ so he would set him down and recite five takbirs over him, until he reached his grave, five times.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: The funeral salat being performed over the deceased
key_terms.خَمْسًا: Five, referring to the number of takbirs
key_terms.سَهْلِ بْنِ حُنَيْفٍ: Sahl ibn Hunayf, the deceased mentioned in the report
key_terms.قَبْرِهِ: His grave, marking the endpoint of the repeated prayers
key_terms.يُكَبِّرُ: He would pronounce the takbir in the funeral prayer

ai.seo_question: Did Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام repeat the funeral prayer for latecomers over Sahl ibn Hunayf?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Amir al-Mu’minin عليه السلام repeated the funeral salat with five takbirs for groups who had missed it over Sahl ibn Hunayf. It reflects the established form of salat al-janazah and preserves a historical report about the care shown in allowing people to participate in the funeral prayer.
